obligation: Corporate (business associate) notice to the Hospital System
trigger: Corporate discovers a breach of unsecured Hospital System PHI on group infrastructure (data centers, file service)
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery (shorter if the BAA says so)
notify: Hospital System Privacy Officer
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - data center and file service incident
clock_starts: Discovery by any corporate employee or agent (164.410(a)(2))

obligation: Corporate (business associate) notice to the Health Plan
trigger: Corporate discovers a breach of unsecured Health Plan PHI
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery
notify: Health Plan Privacy Officer
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - claims core and reporting shares
clock_starts: Discovery by any corporate employee or agent

obligation: Corporate (service provider) notice to the College
trigger: Corporate discovers an incident affecting College customer information on the group file service
deadline: Per the agreement: same day by phone, then in writing
notify: College IT director (Qualified Individual)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - College financial aid and registrar shares

obligation: Florida third-party agent notice to each division (worked example)
trigger: A third-party agent that maintains personal information for a covered entity has a breach
deadline: As expeditiously as practicable, but no later than 10 days following determination of the breach
notify: The Hospital System, the Health Plan, and the College (each a covered entity under the statute for its own data)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - corporate maintains the divisions' data; runs alongside the 164.410 clock

obligation: Hospital System breach notice to patients
trigger: Breach of unsecured PHI (presumed unless the 164.402 four-factor assessment shows a low probability of compromise)
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery
notify: Each affected patient (first-class mail; substitute notice if 10 or more have out-of-date contact information)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - covered entity
clock_starts: Discovery (164.404(a)(2)); the runbook treats the SOC's discovery date as the Hospital System's

obligation: Hospital System notice to HHS (500 or more)
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals
deadline: Contemporaneously with individual notice (within 60 days of discovery)
notify: HHS Secretary via the OCR breach portal
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - expected

obligation: Hospital System media notice
trigger: More than 500 residents of a state or jurisdiction affected
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery
notify: Prominent media outlets in each such state
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - each of the 3 states where more than 500 residents are affected

obligation: Hospital System (business associate) notice to community-connect practices
trigger: Breach of a practice's PHI held in the shared EHR or its reporting extracts
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery, or the BAA term if shorter
notify: Each affected practice's privacy contact
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - 12 practices' patients were in the stolen reporting extracts
notifying_entity: Hospital System (community-connect director with the Privacy Officer)
clock_starts: Discovery by any Hospital System employee or agent

obligation: Hospital System notice content to practices
trigger: Same
deadline: At notification or promptly after as information becomes available
notify: Identification of each affected individual and the information each practice needs for its own 164.404(c) notice
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

obligation: Health Plan breach notice to members
trigger: Breach of unsecured member PHI
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery
notify: Each affected member
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - separate covered entity (no affiliated covered entity designation)
clock_starts: Discovery; the runbook treats the SOC's discovery date as the Health Plan's

obligation: Health Plan notice to HHS (500 or more)
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals
deadline: Contemporaneously with individual notice
notify: HHS Secretary via the OCR breach portal
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - expected

obligation: Health Plan media notice
trigger: More than 500 residents of a state or jurisdiction affected
deadline: Without unreasonable delay and no later than 60 calendar days after discovery
notify: Prominent media outlets in each such state
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - each state over the threshold

obligation: Health Plan (business associate) notice to self-funded employer plans
trigger: Breach of PHI of members of ASO employer plans
deadline: No later than 60 calendar days after discovery, or the BAA term if shorter
notify: Each affected employer group health plan's privacy contact
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - members of 22 of the 40 ASO plans were in the reporting extracts

obligation: People who are both patients and members
trigger: About 70,000 people appear in both the hospital and Health Plan data taken
deadline: Same as each covered entity's clock
notify: Affected individuals; letters may be coordinated
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - each covered entity must still meet its own duty; a coordinated letter must identify both entities

obligation: HIPAA breach log to HHS (fewer than 500)
trigger: A covered entity's breach affects fewer than 500 individuals
deadline: Within 60 days after the end of the calendar year
notify: HHS via the OCR breach portal
applies_at_this_tier: Only if a covered entity's count is under 500

obligation: Law enforcement delay
trigger: Law enforcement states that notice would impede an investigation
deadline: Delay for the period stated in writing; up to 30 days if oral and documented
notify: Hold notices; document the request
applies_at_this_tier: Yes if requested

obligation: State insurance regulator notice (generic)
citation: NAIC Insurance Data Security Model Law #668 sec. 6, as enacted by each state (text varies)
trigger: Cybersecurity event involving the licensee's nonpublic information
deadline: As promptly as possible and no later than 72 hours after determination, in states that enacted it
notify: Insurance commissioner of each state where the Health Plan is licensed and that enacted the model
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - Health Plan, each adopting state of operation (list kept by the Health Plan compliance officer)
clock_starts: Determination that a cybersecurity event occurred

obligation: CMS notification under the Medicare Advantage contract
citation: MA contract and CMS guidance (not verified in this sample)
trigger: Incident affecting MA enrollee data or operations
deadline: Per contract and CMS guidance; confirm before use
notify: CMS through the channel the contract specifies
applies_at_this_tier: Unverified - the Health Plan compliance officer must confirm the current requirement

obligation: Title IV breach report to Federal Student Aid
citation: SAIG Enrollment Agreement (per DCL GEN-15-18); FSA Cybersecurity Breach Intake
trigger: Actual or suspected breach of student financial aid information
deadline: Immediately upon an actual or suspected breach
notify: FSA (CPSSAIG@ed.gov and/or the FSA Cybersecurity Breach Intake Form)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - College financial aid documents on the group file service
notifying_entity: College (financial aid director with the Qualified Individual)

obligation: FTC Safeguards Rule notification event
trigger: Unauthorized acquisition of unencrypted customer information of 500 or more consumers
deadline: As soon as possible, and no later than 30 days after discovery
notify: FTC, using the online form on ftc.gov
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - about 14,000 current and former students' financial aid records
clock_starts: Discovery: first day known to any employee, officer, or other agent other than the attacker (314.4(j)(2))

obligation: FERPA
trigger: Unauthorized disclosure of education records
deadline: FERPA has no breach notification requirement
notify: Not applicable; record the incident in the College's incident file
applies_at_this_tier: No notice duty under FERPA; state breach laws and FSA rules still apply

obligation: State breach notification laws
citation: State breach notification statutes (all 50 states, DC, PR, USVI; Guam 9 GCA Ch. 48)
trigger: Breach of computerized personal information of residents (definitions vary)
deadline: Varies by state
notify: Affected residents; attorney general or regulator where required; consumer reporting agencies above state-set counts
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - apply the law of each state where affected individuals reside (3 hospital states, 5 Health Plan states, and students' states of residence)

obligation: Florida notice to individuals (worked example)
trigger: Breach of personal information (includes medical and health insurance information, and Social Security numbers) of Florida residents
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach (a 15-day extension is possible for good cause, for this individual notice only); a HIPAA-compliant notice is deemed compliant if a copy is timely provided to the Department of Legal Affairs
notify: Affected Florida residents
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - patients, members, and students in Florida

obligation: Florida notice to the Department of Legal Affairs (worked example)
trigger: Breach affecting 500 or more individuals in Florida
deadline: No later than 30 days after determination of the breach
notify: Florida Department of Legal Affairs (Attorney General)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - all three divisions exceed 500 Florida residents in this scenario

obligation: Florida notice to consumer reporting agencies (worked example)
trigger: Notice required to more than 1,000 individuals at one time
deadline: Without unreasonable delay
notify: All nationwide consumer reporting agencies
applies_at_this_tier: Yes

obligation: County EMS and emergency management (diversion and capability)
citation: Hospital emergency preparedness communication plan (42 CFR 482.15(c)(7)); county EMS diversion protocols
trigger: Decision to request ambulance diversion, or loss of capability that affects the community
deadline: At the time of the decision, and at each status change
notify: County EMS dispatch; county emergency management; regional health care coalition; receiving hospitals
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - operational duty under the hospitals' own plan
notifying_entity: Each hospital's incident command, coordinated by the system emergency management director

obligation: EMTALA screening during diversion
trigger: Hospital in diversionary status
deadline: Continuous: a hospital may direct an ambulance not yet on its property elsewhere, but must screen and stabilize anyone who comes to its ED, including an ambulance that arrives anyway
notify: Not a notice; a duty that continues during the incident
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - every ED

obligation: SEC Form 8-K Item 1.05 (material cybersecurity incident)
trigger: The registrant determines a cybersecurity incident is material
deadline: 4 business days after the materiality determination (delay only on a U.S. Attorney General determination)
notify: SEC (public filing)
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - Cris Santos Company Holdings is an SEC registrant
clock_starts: Materiality determination, made without unreasonable delay

obligation: SEC Reg S-K Item 106 annual disclosure
trigger: Annual report
deadline: Next Form 10-K
notify: Investors
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - describe risk management and governance; lessons from the incident may inform it

obligation: OFAC sanctions check before any ransom payment
citation: OFAC Updated Advisory on Potential Sanctions Risks for Facilitating Ransomware Payments (Sept. 21, 2021); 31 CFR ch. V
trigger: Considering a ransomware payment
deadline: Before any payment; full and timely reporting to law enforcement or CISA is a mitigating factor
notify: OFAC (license if sanctioned party); FBI or CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - all U.S. persons

obligation: Voluntary report to law enforcement and CISA
trigger: Ransomware or extortion
deadline: As soon as practicable (Day 0 to 1 target)
notify: FBI field office or IC3; CISA
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - recommended

obligation: CIRCIA covered cyber incident and ransom payment reports
trigger: Covered cyber incident or ransom payment
deadline: Proposed: 72 hours (incident); 24 hours after ransom payment
notify: CISA
applies_at_this_tier: NOT YET REQUIRED: final rule not published as of 2026-09-25; reporting is voluntary until then. As proposed, it would cover all 9 hospitals (100 or more beds) and the College (Title IV)

obligation: Cyber insurance claim notice
trigger: Suspected security incident
deadline: Per policy; call the carrier hotline before engaging vendors
notify: Carrier breach hotline
applies_at_this_tier: Yes - contractual, not legal

obligation: Part 2 record breach
trigger: Breach of Part 2 records
deadline: Same as HIPAA
notify: Patients, HHS, media
applies_at_this_tier: No - no hospital is a Part 2 program; recheck whether Part 2 records received from outside programs were in the stolen extracts

obligation: FTC Health Breach Notification Rule
trigger: Breach by a non-HIPAA personal health record vendor
deadline: Within 60 calendar days after discovery
notify: Individuals, FTC, media
applies_at_this_tier: No - the health divisions act as HIPAA covered entities and business associates, which 318.1 excludes; the College runs no personal health record

obligation: Covered telecommunications / Kaspersky article / FASCSA article discovered
citation: FAR 52.204-25(d) (Section 889); FAR 52.204-23(c); FAR 52.204-30; FAR 52.240-91(h) in awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation
trigger: Contractor identifies covered telecommunications equipment or services, a Kaspersky covered article, or a FASCSA covered article
deadline: Within 1 business day for covered telecommunications equipment or services (52.204-25(d)); within 3 business days for a Kaspersky covered article (52.204-23(c)) and for a FASCSA covered article (52.204-30); further report within 10 business days in each case. Under FAR 52.240-91(h) (new awards under an agency's FAR Part 40 class deviation): one report within 72 hours, to https://dibnet.dod.mil for DoD or to the contracting officer for other agencies; a further report within 72 hours of finding missing information.
notify: Contracting officer
applies_at_this_tier: Only if the group holds federal contracts or subcontracts with these clauses (Medicare participation and Title IV participation are not procurement contracts); confirm with the Group General Counsel
